• Your childs personal interests Lets face it, costumes can be expensive if you are going down that retail rabbit hole (been there done that) - best thing to do for kids under 6 is find something they can use again for dress up play, that way if you are spending the $$ on it you will get more than just one nights use out of it. Ideas could be: Nurse, Doctor, Fireman, Police or a Scientist

  • Your budget You don't always have to spend the big bucks, unless you want to. I don't go to thrift stores usually but I do check them out in the run up to Halloween for prop clothes etc and sometimes they actually have kids costumes still in the bag and unused for a fraction of the cost. If you don't mind ones that are unbagged and just used once they are also available - sometimes with accessories and sometimes not.

  • Don't discount the "classics" The ghosts, vampires, witches, pumpkins etc Most of these don't go out of style and lets face it they are a hell of a lot friendlier on the wallets of us parents than all the new TV & movie characters.

  • Make it yourself This one can go either way - some material depending on what you go for, could be fairly cheap or could be totally expensive. It also hinges on if you can sew or even have access to a sewing machine. Other things you could have around the house as part of your kids wardrobe, we live out in the sticks so if my son wanted to be a farmer it would be easy and cheap for me to accomplish with items he already has as clothes.

At the end of it all, think outside the box - some of the best & memorable ones I have seen have been handmade and not come from a big box chain store!
